claim: at lam=1/10, gamma=6 (above the shore, so negatives are guaranteed) the NEGATIVE Gegenbauer coefficients of q are confined to a low band: the largest negative index divided by sqrt(N) sits at 3.93..4.07 across N = 199..1599, while its share of the spectrum falls from 0.286 to 0.098
why_it_matters: the outside memorandum's remaining gap is a possible negative BULK coefficient at m ~ rho N. These measurements show the offending set living at the sqrt(N) scale, i.e. m/N -> 0, with no sign of bulk offending. Evidence, not proof: the constant near 4 is stable but drifts slightly downward at the largest N, and this is a single (lam, gamma) line.

other_lines_measured.note: same N = 199,399,799; the constant depends on (lam,gamma) and still drifts upward on those lines -- NOT a law yet

REFINEMENT_same_day.what_changed: the sqrt(N) localisation is a property of the PHYSICAL regime (gamma at or near the shore), not a universal law in gamma. Tested at gamma = 30 with lam = 1/10 -- eight times the shore -- the bad set is a THIRD of the spectrum at N = 1599 and shrinks only like N^-0.37, and max/sqrt(gamma N) drifts 1.90 -> 2.34 -> 2.50 instead of settling. So neither sqrt(N) nor sqrt(gamma N) is the law.

at_the_shore_which_is_what_matters.reading: at the shore the offending set occupies a vanishing fraction of the spectrum in all three families, falling roughly like N^-0.48 .. N^-0.72. The absolute scale is near 4 sqrt(N) and drifting slowly downward.

REFINEMENT_same_day.honest_status: the qualitative claim -- the bad set is a vanishing fraction of the spectrum at the shore, so the bulk does not offend -- holds in every physical cell measured. The quantitative claim -- a clean sqrt(N) law with a constant -- does NOT hold once gamma is pushed well above the shore, and is withdrawn.
